source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata
why_relevant: Company register: resolves vendor legal names, local subsidiaries of regional integrators, ownership changes and dissolutions. Essential for interpreting an archived case study whose vendor no longer exists under that name.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — 'E-services and digital infrastructure as a response to COVID-19' (EU-funded, with MJU)
why_relevant: Donor-implemented digital projects publish results, partner and often contractor names that the ministry itself omits. UNDP procurement notices for these projects are a second, parallel channel naming e-service/e-payment implementers.

source_name: gov.me document repository (dokumenta) — strategies, action plans, gazette copies
why_relevant: The government's own GUID-addressed document store holds strategy PDFs, action plans and reporting on their implementation (izvještaj o realizaciji), which are where completed e-payment components and their status are enumerated.

source_name: eKontrola / Provjeri uplate — companion state payment control systems
why_relevant: Second-order components of the NS NAT e-payment stack, confirmed from the gov.me description page. Distinct subsystems often mean distinct suppliers or modules; their page assets and login banners can reveal the platform in use.

source_name: Wikipedia — Ministry of Public Administration, Digital Society and Media (Montenegro)
why_relevant: Tracks the ministry's repeated renaming/merging (MJU / MJUDDM / current form), which is the main reason older digital-agenda documents and their URLs go dead. Gives the alias list needed to search archives correctly.

source_name: Zbornik radova Pravnog fakulteta UCG — 'Digitalna transformacija javne uprave u Crnoj Gori kroz prizmu EU integracija'
why_relevant: Academic review of Montenegro's public-administration digitalisation with comparative Western Balkans framing; useful for a referenced inventory of programmes and institutions, including ones whose primary pages are gone.

source_name: CBCG — Fiskalni agent / državni zapisi
why_relevant: Shows CBCG's role as fiscal agent and the state-securities operations it runs; the settlement/auction infrastructure behind it is a discrete IT procurement area adjacent to the payments stack.

source_name: CBCG statistics on the central bank payment system (time series)
why_relevant: Long-run volume/value series; step changes in card, instant or RTGS volumes date platform migrations and help pin down when a vendor's (now-deleted) case study would have been published.

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka, OTP Group) - Novosti / press detail pages
why_relevant: CKB is the largest bank in Montenegro (OTP Group). Its 'Novosti' items are the primary public channel where product launches and, occasionally, the technology partner behind them are named. URL pattern novosti-detalj?nid=<int> is an enumerable ID sequence, which makes systematic backfill of the full news archive feasible.

source_name: CKB consolidated audited financial statements (IFRS notes) - PDF
why_relevant: Audited annual statements of ME banks carry 'nematerijalna ulaganja / softver' (intangibles/software) notes, capex on IT, and sometimes operating-lease or service-contract disclosures that indirectly size IT spend and occasionally name suppliers. For privately-held systemic banks with no public procurement, this is one of very few quantitative windows onto technology investment.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica - Finansijski izvještaji
why_relevant: NLB Podgorica (NLB Group, ~EUR 1.03bn assets) publishes financial reports; the same intangibles/software-capex logic applies. NLB is also a repeat digital-channel buyer (NLB Klik, mKlik, ProKlik), so year-on-year IT capex moves are a useful procurement-cycle proxy.

source_name: Erste banka Crna Gora - Press section
why_relevant: Erste ME maintains an explicit Press section ('materials to help in preparing reports about Erste banka'). Erste Group subsidiaries typically issue launch communications for digital channels and card products, which is where a technology partner would be named in this market.

source_name: Hipotekarna Banka - Obavještenja / Saopštenje za javnost
why_relevant: Hipotekarna is the #2 bank in ME by assets (14.84% share, 2025) and one of the most digitally active — its announcements track product and channel launches. The URL pattern /obavjestenja/saopstenje-za-javnost-<int> is a sequential slug, making full archive reconstruction realistic.

source_name: Adriatic Bank - News (EN/SR)
why_relevant: Adriatic Bank runs an explicit bilingual News section and has been an early-mover announcer (e.g. bringing Apple Pay to Montenegro, reported March 2025). Smaller challenger banks communicate launches more aggressively than incumbents, so this is a high-signal, low-volume feed for new-technology entry into the ME market.

source_name: Zapad banka AD Podgorica - corporate site / About bank
why_relevant: 5th-largest bank in ME (5.52% share, 2025). Bilingual corporate site; the About/News areas are the only public channel for any technology-partner disclosure by this bank. Low volume but must be covered for completeness of the buyer-side panel.

source_name: Universal Capital Bank AD Podgorica - corporate site
why_relevant: 8th-largest ME bank (~EUR 361m assets, 4.98% share). Named by CBCG as a participant in the national instant-payments rollout, so its own channel is a place where the instant-payments technology stack and its supplier could surface.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica - corporate site & social channels
why_relevant: 7th-largest ME bank (5.04% share). Confirmed buyer of at least two named suppliers (Fleka for web+online banking, Gecko HRM for HR), so its launch communications and social posts are a proven vendor-reveal channel. Its Instagram/Facebook feeds appear more active than the website news section.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro - Elektronsko bankarstvo & terms PDFs
why_relevant: The bank's e-banking product pages and the associated 'Opšti uslovi za e-banking' PDF describe the channel, its components and sometimes the third-party service centre behind it. Terms-and-conditions documents are an underrated vendor-reveal channel because they must name the operator of the service.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore - Elektronsko bankarstvo pages
why_relevant: Oldest ME bank (founded 1901). Its e-banking pages and app describe the digital channel; the Android package id of its app (hr.asseco.android.jimba.prvabanka) independently identifies Asseco as the channel supplier. Bank product pages plus store metadata together give attribution the bank never states in prose.

source_name: App-store listings for ME bank apps (Google Play / Apple App Store) - package-id vendor fingerprinting
why_relevant: HIGHEST-YIELD INDIRECT CHANNEL FOUND IN THIS CELL. Android package ids leak the actual software supplier even when the bank never names one. Confirmed in this pass: hr.asseco.android.jimba.prvabanka (Prva banka -> Asseco), hr.asseco.android.jimba.zbme.production (Ziraat ME -> Asseco), hr.asseco.android.jimba.nlbcrnagoracorp.me (NLB ProKlik -> Asseco), com.logate.hbklik (Hipotekarna mHB klik -> Logate), me.fleka.hipotekarna and me.fleka.lovcen (Fleka), com.provisionpay.softpos.hipotekarna (Hipotekarna MojPOS -> ProvisionPay softPOS), com.halcom.mobile.hybrid.* (Halcom). Release notes and changelogs additionally date each platform migration.

source_name: Logate (Podgorica) - CX360 banking CRM client roster & case studies
why_relevant: Logate is a Podgorica-based software house (founded 2006) whose own marketing page names its ME bank installed base explicitly: CX360 deployed at Erste Montenegro, NLB Podgorica, CKB (OTP), Hipotekarna, Lovćen and Prva banka (plus AIK). It also documents a Connect contact-centre video-channel upgrade for Hipotekarna. A single vendor page resolves the buyer-side attribution for six of the ten banks in this cell.

source_name: Fleka (Podgorica digital agency) - bank web & online-banking portfolio
why_relevant: Fleka's portfolio states it built the online banking (web/app) and website for Lovćen banka, and its package namespace (me.fleka.lovcen, me.fleka.hipotekarna) shows it also ships apps for Hipotekarna. Local digital agencies are a distinct supplier tier below the core-banking vendors and are almost never named by the banks themselves.

source_name: Gecko HRM - Lovćen banka case study
why_relevant: A named, written case study describing how Lovćen banka modernised HR operations and compliance with Gecko HRM. Demonstrates the general pattern for this cell: when a ME bank will not disclose a supplier, the supplier publishes a case study naming the bank. Also extends the actor map beyond core banking into adjacent enterprise software bought by banks.

source_name: UBCG - Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (Association of Montenegrin Banks)
why_relevant: Industry association whose member directory carries each bank's address, phone and official website — a clean, maintained pointer set for the buyer-side panel. Associations also host conferences and publish member communications, which is where joint technology initiatives (instant payments, cards, AML tooling) tend to be described collectively.

source_name: SCMN / Komisija za tržište kapitala - Emitenti (issuer disclosures)
why_relevant: Several ME banks (e.g. Hipotekarna banka) are listed issuers and must file periodic and ad-hoc disclosures with the capital-market authority. Issuer filings are a mandatory-publication channel that bypasses the banks' voluntary PR entirely — material contracts and significant investments can appear here first.

source_name: ME bank LinkedIn company pages (CKB, Erste ME, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, NLB, Logate)
why_relevant: In this market LinkedIn is frequently where a launch is announced with the partner tagged, even when the bank's own website carries nothing. Vendor and bank employees also post project milestones (an observed example: a Lovćen banka post by a named employee). Job postings on the same pages leak the technology stack being hired for.

source_name: ME bank Facebook / Instagram pages
why_relevant: For the smaller ME banks (Lovćen, Zapad, Universal Capital) the social feed is more current than the corporate website and is often the only place a product launch is announced at all. Local-language posts are the realistic first-disclosure channel for retail-facing technology rollouts.
